newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- Bias in T-bonds still pointing upward.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- Bias in T-bonds still pointing upward.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond options trading continued to reflect a bullish directional bias Wednesday as the underlying futures climbed to another 7-1/2-month high.
"The mentality is, this is free money. The trend is still okay to buy," said one options trader on the bond floor.
Traders said put-selling strategies predominated early, with call buying seen to a lesser degree than was evident Tuesday.
"We're seeing a lot of put selling as a way to capture premium," the bond floor trader said.
Short put positions are favored when volatility appears excessive.
Implied volatilities on bond options were well bid at the open, then values were shaved through the day as the market digested Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.

Greenspan, in his semiannual address delivered to the House late Tuesday and the Senate this morning, said the Fed would ultimately have to change interest rates, but for now, U.S. growth was slowing.

Implied volatility for September Treasury bonds opened where it settled, at 8.2 percent, then slipped to around 8.0 percent by the end of the session as futures retreated from their highs. December was quoted at 8.5 percent late.
"There has been some buying of calls on the way down and some profit-taking in futures," said a broker.
Early in the session, a dealer bought 2,000 of the 116-00 calls while selling double the number of 118-00 calls. "They expect a slow rally," said the first trader.
Anticipation of upcoming economic data should underpin vols heading into next week, traders said.

U.S. durable goods orders for June are due out Friday, and analysts look for a gain of 1.4 percent following a 0.6 percent decline in May. Existing home sales, also due Friday, are forecast to slow to a 4.19 million annualized rate from 4.24 million previously.

Next week brings the second-quarter employment cost index Tuesday and advance second-quarter gross domestic product Thursday, followed on Friday by the July employment report. There is also a quarterly refunding comprising three- and 10-year notes and 30-year bonds.
In Eurodollar options, one trading desk late in the session quoted volatilities steady on the day at about 8.6 percent in December and 10.7 percent in March after early gains in those values faded.
A large call purchase combined with straddle and strangle buying to temporarily boost front-month vols early, a Eurodollar broker said.
